newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECHS PROTEST CHINESE DISSIDENT'S SENTENCE.
newsitem.headline: CZECHS PROTEST CHINESE DISSIDENT'S SENTENCE.

text.p: The Czech Republic on Thursday officially protested against a Chinese court's 11-year prison sentence issued to leading dissident Wang Dan who was accused of plotting to overthrow Beijing's Communist government.
The Czech Foreign Ministry said in a statement that it invited China's top diplomat in Prague, charge' d'affaires Wang Zizhen, to the ministry on Thursday where a statement of protest was read.

"(In this matter) the Czech Republic expresses its dissatisfaction over the conduct of the trial and the judgement carried out," the statement said according a text issued by the Czech Foreign Ministry.

It said that although there were differences in traditions of understanding questions of human rights in different regions, "there exists certain universal principles of maintaining human rights which are necessary to respect."
Wang, 27, was sentenced to 11 years in prison on Wednesday after a brief hearing which Chinese official media called a model of fairness with no connection to human rights issues.
International human right activists condemned the trial as a sham and the verdict as a travesty.
The Czech statement said freedom of speech is a "basic civic freedom" and that its criminalisation was "a violation of elementary human rights."

Czech President Vaclav Havel, a former leading dissident imprisoned several times by a hard-line Communist government before its fall in 1989, angered China last year with a highly publicised meeting with Taiwan's Premier Lien Chan.
Havel has also expressed regret that Taiwan, which Bejing regards as a renegade province, was not a U.N. member, and asked for mutual respect between the mainland and the island.
The Czechs officially however still only recognise Communist China as a sovereign state and not Taiwan.
